GOV.reason: Repeated cash-flow classification/reconciliation weaknesses and IPO implementation/co-mingling comments support 4, not a fraud finding. Contrary evidence: an unmodified audit, director funding, actual equity receipt and reported correction of temporary mutual-fund parking. This assesses stewardship, not an extra haircut on every factor.

MOAT.reason: Own products are 33% of sales and channel expansion is real. Contrary: 67% remains trading/services, customers are concentrated and designs/channels are contestable. No verified retention, premium or CAC economics establishes a durable barrier. Four reflects the observed business structure, not disclosure volume.

REV.reason: Five-year CAGR 34.19% starts at 9; FY2026 grew 24.65% and own products 60.46%. Contrary: ten-year CAGR is 18.01%, with an earlier contraction and business-model change. No trajectory adjustment is added; Medium confidence and relevant brand-history ceiling cap REV at 8.

DUR.reason: Home categories and announced offline access offer growth avenues, with ₹44.25 crore actually received. Contrary: new nutraceutical operations are unproven, category funding fell from ₹35 crore proposed to ₹6 crore, and Centro is not backlog. Five reflects useful but constrained access.

CAP.reason: NS. FY2026 operating IC ₹80.1357 crore and financing proxy ₹79.6643 crore reconcile, but brand-cost composition, segment returns and immature office/CWIP obscure incremental economics. Profit growth is positive contrary evidence. Three-/five-year accounting proxies are retained, not misrepresented as project returns.

CASH.reason: Four is a bounded assessment: both FY2026 CFO variants leave three-year conversion below .8×, while inventory/receivables and weak supplier credit absorb funds. Contrary: CFO is positive and five-year conversion reaches .878× under one variant. Exact CFO remains disputed; capex explains FCF, not CFO. No persistent ≤3 override applies.

BAL.reason: Five: ₹44.25 crore received materially exceeds March debt ₹13.04 crore, the director loan is interest-free and no default is reported. Contrary: current cash/deployment and maturities are unverified and linked stress breaches cash. G3 Hold alone does not erase this bounded historical funding evidence.

EXEC.reason: Five: revenue/brand growth, actual subsidiary incorporation and a disclosed Blisshome launch show delivery. Contrary: office completion was 80 days late, most proposed preferential capital was not received, Centro unit economics are unverified and Bummer is nonbinding. Observable milestones replace invented guidance.

EARN.reason: NS. FY2026 PAT grew 20.62% and operating EBITDA is positive. Contrary: brand capitalization is material and cash-flow/segment-profit conflicts prevent reliable normalized profit and per-share quality. The expense-all-brand stress is not substituted for factual earnings.

R.reason: NS. Complete conditional models do not establish a supported base return while normalization and current cash remain unresolved. Mechanical −0.36% is not scored as validated, nor replaced by a neutral 5. Bull upside is retained as contrary scenario evidence.

D.reason: Three: the raise provides a buffer, but linked collection/inventory delay and margin stress breach cash and imply about 84% price impairment even with uncommitted rescue. This is scenario-based resilience at ₹242, not a default allegation. Recovery is possible if collections and margins normalize.

P.reason: Three: reported P/E 29.65× becomes 51.69× in the brand-expense sensitivity; at 12×/18% margin, the 15% hurdle requires 38.42% growth, above five-year 34.19% and current 24.65%. Contrary: three-year growth was 46.59% and the bull scenario meets the hurdle. No catalyst bonus is added.

L.reason: Starting 5 from 9.54 theoretical exit days, explicitly reduced to 4 for 400-share lots and only six of the latest twenty sessions supporting one whole lot at 5% participation. Contrary: all sixty sessions traded. Spread/surveillance are unknown, so implementation is conditional, not automatically impossible.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved financial reliability, rather than a supported purchase at ₹242. Encompass has scaled reported revenue and received ₹44.25 crore of fresh equity. However, its FY2026 cash-flow and segment-profit disclosures do not reconcile, and brand-cost capitalization materially affects economic earnings. BQS is NS with 88% coverage and a 4.38–5.46 mathematical bound; GQS is NS with 70% coverage and a 4.90–7.60 bound; IAS is NS with 40% coverage and a 1.90–7.30 bound. These are not confidence intervals or ranking substitutes. [E01–E09]
The positive case is owned-brand growth and distribution expansion. The rebuttal is that 67% of revenue still comes from trading/services, cash conversion is weak, and roughly 30× reported earnings demands durable per-share compounding. The conditional base model returns −0.36% annually; a strong bull case only reaches 15.07%. Neither is a validated price target. The unreceived ₹51 crore and proposed Bummer acquisition are not treated as completed funding or operating facts. [E09,E11,E13,E21–E24]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Identity: Encompass Design India Limited, NSE SME ENCOMPAS, ISIN INE433T01015. Research cutoff: 20 October 2026, Asia/Kolkata date basis. Sources were retrieved on 21 October, but only information available by the cutoff is used. Valuation quote: official 19 October close/last ₹242, from one 400-share trade. Horizon: 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031; nominal INR, 15% annual equity hurdle before investor taxes. The ₹5 lakh liquidity reference is not an allocation recommendation. [E19]
Accounts use Indian GAAP/Accounting Standards, not Ind AS. FY2026 standalone is the latest verified financial perimeter. The 66.67%-owned Longevity Plan subsidiary was incorporated in July 2026; future consolidated scope matters. No comparable FY2027 H1 result or reliable TTM is available in the reviewed cutoff record. [E01,E12]
G1 Integrity: Conditional, not Fail. G2 Reliability: Hold — unresolved, because signed cash-flow versions and segment gross profit conflict. G3 Funding: Hold — unresolved current cash/debt bridge, not an observed default. G4 Tradability: Conditional, because historical turnover is available but lots, spreads and current restrictions affect execution. Confidence is High for headline disclosed statements, issued shares and market archives; Medium for growth decomposition and bounded governance/balance-sheet judgments; Low for normalized earnings, capital returns and current funding. Overall investment confidence is Low. G3 Hold alone does not erase independently supported quality factors.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors: GOV 4, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 5, CAP NS, CASH 4, BAL 5, EXEC 5, EARN NS, R NS, D 3, P 3, L 4. Supporting and contrary facts are retained in factor_audit; each factor is assigned once.
BQS known contribution = .20×4 + .20×4 + .12×8 + .10×5 + .10×4 + .08×5 + .08×5 = 4.26. Missing CAP weight is .12. Bound = [4.38,5.46], displayed 4.4–5.5; coverage 88%, final NS. GQS known contribution = .40×8 + .20×5 + .10×4 = 4.60. Missing EARN/CAP weight .30 gives [4.90,7.60], coverage 70%, final NS. IAS known contribution = .20×3 + .10×3 + .10×4 = 1.30. Q and R weight .60 gives [1.90,7.30], coverage 40%, final NS. Q must reuse final BQS, not GQS or a midpoint.
Missing weights are not redistributed. No numeric override is triggered: GOV is above 3; G1/G3 do not fail; CASH is 4 and CAP is NS. GOV or MOAT ±1 changes BQS's known contribution by ±.20 each; DUR ±1 changes GQS by ±.20. The material G2 hold bars ranking. Exact arithmetic, bounds and confidence are in model/score_audit.json. [E02–E25]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Encompass sells home/lifestyle products under Stoa Paris, Quirkloom and Small Batch, trades/distributes other products, and provides consultancy/enablement services. FY2026 own-product revenue was ₹22.4662 crore (33.0%), trading ₹39.8195 crore (58.5%) and services ₹5.8343 crore (8.6%). Exports were ₹0.6325 crore, under 1%. Product revenue is recognized on delivery/dispatch and risk transfer, net of returns, GST and discounts; services follow milestones. This is not a pure brand-licensing or software-annuity business. [E01,E13]
Cash is committed to merchandise, supplier advances, channels and brand building. Buyers choose design, price and availability; partners choose enablement execution. Owned-brand monetization is the promising profit pool, but inconsistent segment disclosures prevent assigning all group margins to brands. Revenue less disclosed material/trading costs is ₹36.2787 crore before employee and other expenses, a contribution proxy rather than reliable segment profit. [E03,E07,E13]
Blisshome launched on 26 March 2026. Longevity Plan had no initial turnover and enters nutraceuticals, not an established profit engine. US/Dubai subsidiaries were approved, but operational incorporation was not verified. Bummer remains nonbinding. No revenue from these initiatives is inserted into historical organic growth. [E11–E15]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Brand/design → named products and 33% own-product revenue → possible repeat purchasing and distribution → failure if paid acquisition costs, marketplace dependence or imitation absorb returns. No independently verified premium, cohort retention, CAC/payback or defined market-share denominator establishes a strong moat. SKU/customer counts are management claims, not audited customer economics. [E13,E15]
Distribution/enablement → service revenue and a Centro relationship → possible channel access → failure if partners multisource or insource. The Centro disclosure expressly says the arrangement is not a purchase order. Capable entrants can source home textiles and buy online advertising; precise entry cost/time is ND. Customer concentration strengthens buyer risk: the prospectus top-ten measure is 66.53% for FY2025 and 71.50% for H1 FY2026, with an amount-received/revenue definition caveat. [E14,E15]
Welspun Living, Indo Count and Himatsingka provide home-textile/brand context and stronger industrial-scale comparisons. Export manufacturing and integrated assets make them imperfect matches for Encompass's blended model. No current quantitative peer-multiple median, or unsupported stronger/weaker investment ranking, is fabricated. Useful brands are not yet evidence of durable excess returns: MOAT 4. [E25]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Audited operating revenue, FY2016 through FY2026, ₹ crore: 13.0079, 17.3012, 19.5065, 25.7674, 14.1517, 15.6581, 17.6486, 21.6247, 40.0418, 54.6494, 68.1201. The exact intervals give 10-year CAGR 18.01%, five-year 34.19%, and three-year 46.59%. FY2026 growth is 24.65%. Revenue additions in FY2024/25/26 are ₹18.4171/14.6076/13.4707 crore. The FY2020 contraction and later business-model change are relevant cycle context, not a blanket small-base penalty. [E02]
Audited FY2026 categories show own products +60.46%, trading +12.02% and services +14.35%. Presentation brand growth of 56% uses an unreconciled basis and is not substituted. Price, volume, currency, new-customer and organic/acquisition decomposition remain ND. No completed Bummer or Longevity revenue is credited. No current interim/TTM rate is invented or seasonal quarter annualized. [E11–E15]
REV starts at 9 under the ≥30% five-year CAGR band, with no discretionary trajectory adjustment. It is capped at 8 because relevant owned-brand history is shorter and decomposition confidence is Medium. Independently measured industry-relative growth or market-share gains are unavailable and receive no bonus.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Accessible avenues include consumer categories, offline distribution, warehouse/IT capacity and enablement services. Actual equity receipts expanded funding, but new-category allocation fell from the proposed ₹35 crore to ₹6 crore. Centro access, overseas approvals and nonbinding Bummer are options, not backlog or commissioned profitable capacity. [E09,E11–E15]
A unit/cohort forecast cannot be established from headline SKU/customer counts. No store count, utilization or TAM share is invented. The conditional base uses growth of 20/20/18/15/12% to reach ₹149.09 crore, an assumption rather than supported guidance. Its 18% economic EBITDA margin expenses ordinary brand-building cash; ONWC expands with revenue, maintenance physical/software capex is 2% of sales, incremental new-category cash losses total ₹6 crore, and warehouse/IT uses ₹3.7 crore. [E21]
FY2026 ONWC is ₹27.1496 crore and operating invested capital ₹80.1357 crore, including office, CWIP and intangibles. The financing proxy ₹79.6643 crore reconciles through statutory assets, income tax, gratuity and deferred tax. Three-/five-year incremental proxies are 20.94%/21.95%: NOPAT changes ₹14.3968/13.6799 crore over financing-capital changes ₹68.7667/62.3283 crore. Brand capitalization, margin recovery and immature assets prevent interpreting them as project returns. Lagged commissioned-asset profits are not separable. A 13–17% nominal INR cost-of-capital range is illustrative context, not an estimated WACC. CAP remains NS; high current ROCE is not a neutral CAP score. [E06–E08]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Actual allotment tables support transaction-only pro forma promoter ownership of about 57.93%, not a certified October free float. The encumbrance declaration covers the year to March 2026, not current pledges. Preferential shares were issued at ₹250, 3.31% above the ₹242 quote; actual shares increased 12.48%. Raising equity is not itself minority abuse, but the unreceived ₹51 crore cannot fund the plan. [E09,E16,E24]
Allocation concerns include the office purchase, brand capitalization, revised objects, co-mingling and an 80-day office implementation delay. The June monitoring table shows IPO objects fully funded; a stale management paragraph and inconsistent cash-flow presentation weaken control confidence. Contrary evidence includes an unmodified audit/CARO, no reported borrowing default, shareholder approval for object variation, and real fresh cash. GOV is 4, not a fraud finding. [E03,E04,E07,E10,E16]
FY2026 RPTs include an interest-free director loan of ₹1.3439 crore, ₹1.19 crore taken and ₹1.69 crore repaid; remuneration and related professional fees are disclosed. FY2022's ₹0.831 crore branding/advertisement reversal with OTH Online is not described as an arm's-length asset sale. Preference-conversion/share-transfer record corrections and short statutory delays appear in the prospectus. The GST notice is contested, not an adjudicated liability; later resolution is ND. [E17,E18]
Promises versus delivery: office target 31 March → completion 19 June 2026; Blisshome launch disclosed; Centro launch announced without independently verified store economics; Longevity incorporated 8 July without an operating track record; planned ₹95.25 crore preferential raise → ₹44.25 crore received; Bummer remains conditional. Auditor resignation or changes beyond reviewed records are not inferred. EXEC is 5. [E09–E15]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY2024/25/26, ₹ crore: revenue 40.0418/54.6494/68.1201; calculated operating EBITDA 11.2137/16.8643/20.7557; EBIT 9.4868/14.5870/17.8921; PAT 6.8790/10.7938/13.0191; CFO 6.5029/4.7380/6.2055 using the May FY2026 version, versus annual-report FY2026 CFO 9.4216; capex 6.3517/9.9048/36.8387. FY2026 PAT margin is 19.11%, EBITDA margin 30.47%. Normalized PAT is NS. Weighted EPS ₹11.15 differs from ₹8.16 on current issued shares; unadjusted pre-bonus FY2025 EPS ₹276.96 is not comparable growth. [E01–E08,E24]
Annual cash flow adds ₹3.3296 crore labelled income taxes paid to ₹6.0920 crore cash generated, and places ₹32.8640 crore share capital/premium in investing. The May filing reports CFO ₹6.2055 crore; its integrated filing has different adjustment labels. Both close at ₹15.1635 crore cash. FY2025 had a similar equity-proceeds classification corrected in restatement. Segment gross profit also conflicts: annual ₹28.3019 crore versus May ₹36.2787 crore. These are specific reconciliation failures, not proof that cash is missing. [E03,E04,E13]
Average-balance receivable days rose 32.5 → 45.8 → 56.4 using total revenue. Inventory days on the disclosed material-cost proxy rose 115.4 → 155.6 in FY2025/26; payable days fell 16.8 → 9.0. This proxy cash cycle widened 144.4 → 203.0 days and excludes labor/overhead, so it is not a full-cost cycle. Disputed receivables ₹0.7503 crore include ₹0.6345 crore over three years. Three-year CFO/PAT is only 56.84–67.32% across disclosed variants; five-year 76.68–87.83% is contrary context. Expansion capex explains weak FCF, not CFO. [E05,E06]
Intangibles ₹23.0562 crore and CWIP ₹7.3920 crore remain in invested capital. Expensing all brand additions, reversing brand amortization and removing other income gives a sensitivity PAT of ₹7.4691 crore at 25% tax, not a factual restatement. FY2021–22 tangible equity was negative. Current debt maturities are counted once; no invented lease liabilities or unrestricted-cash certification is inserted. [E07,E08,E17]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Market cap is ₹386.0758 crore at ₹242 and 15,953,544 actual shares. FY2026 PAT/current shares gives EPS ₹8.16 and P/E 29.65×; the expense-all-brand sensitivity gives 51.69×. P/B 4.72× uses March equity only, not post-preferential book value. EV ₹383.9510 crore using March cash/debt is a dated diagnostic, not live EV. The explicit conditional October bridge gives EV ₹354.6910 crore and 17.09× reported FY2026 EBITDA. No brand/office book assets are added again to terminal enterprise value. [E08,E09,E24]
Conditional opening cash = March ₹15.1635 + received equity ₹44.25 − verified April–June IPO deployment ₹4.99 − assumed other interim use ₹10 = ₹44.4235 crore, not an observed bank balance. The ₹4.71 crore WC deployment enters opening ONWC once. Debt repayment is ₹10 crore in year one and ₹3.0387 crore in year two. Legacy tax ₹3.1411 crore and gratuity ₹0.4421 crore are paid once. The residual March capital commitment assumed open is ₹0.785 crore after the verified ₹0.28 crore spend. [E06,E09,E10]
New-category losses are ₹3 crore in each of years one/two; warehouse/IT spend is ₹3.7 crore in year one. The ₹20.55 crore WC allocation is not a second expense: forecast ONWC absorption uses cash once. The ₹4 crore GCP amount is retained as a cash floor, not both spent and added back. Ordinary brand spending is already in the economic margin; only physical/software maintenance capex is deducted separately. Debt, interest, taxes, dilution and terminal cash reconcile annually. [E21]
Conditional base growth 20/20/18/15/12%, 18% economic margin and 12× exit gives ₹237.68 terminal value and −0.36% annual return. Bull growth 30/30/25/20/15%, 20–22% margins and 16× gives ₹488.29 and 15.07%. Base entry around ₹118.17 meets the 15% hurdle only under these assumptions, not as a fair-value fact or buy limit. A 1% cost on each side is shown separately. Supported R/IAS remain NS. [E21]
At 18% margin and 12×, a 15% return requires 38.42% revenue CAGR to ₹346.10 crore; 12%/18% hurdles require 34.37%/42.43%. At 16×, 15% requires 30.22%; at 8× no funded solution reaches 15% within the modeled domain. Growth × multiple and interim-cash-use sensitivities are provided. Normalized earnings and dated asset/funding bridges are cross-checks; no DCF terminal-value share is claimed because a DCF is not used. [E23,E24]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
Permanent-impairment risk is High, not an assertion of default. Linked stress uses revenue growth −10/0/5/5/5%, economic margins 4/7/9/10/10%, 90 extra collection days and 90 extra inventory days, plus ₹20 crore interim cash use. Cash turns negative in year one: peak actual deficit is ₹5.58 crore and the gap to a ₹4 crore cash floor is ₹9.58 crore. The primary path is unfunded, so an executable bear IRR is withheld. Mechanical terminal price ₹34.65 cannot imply survival without funding. [E06,E22]
A separate, uncommitted equity-rescue counterfactual at ₹121 per share raises ₹9.58 crore and dilutes owners. It produces ₹38.74 terminal value, about 84% price impairment and −30.68% annual return. It is not available financing or a refinancing promise. Receivable/brand write-offs or withdrawal of supplier support could worsen recovery. A legal default date cannot be inferred without current maturity documents. [E22]
Recovery requires collections, productive brand/office investment and profitable growth without adverse issuance. Bummer is a separate sensitivity only: ₹0.65 crore cash, ₹4 crore shares at an assumed ₹250, and ₹2.93 crore annual cash-burn proxy with no positive acquired value reduce base IRR to −1.37%. These are neither signed final terms nor a forecast of actual cash burn. [E09,E11,E21]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Five-year 5×/10× share-price outcomes require 37.97%/58.49% annual shareholder returns. At unchanged shares, terminal equity would be ₹1,930.38/₹3,860.76 crore. At 18% economic EBITDA margin, 12× exit and zero net cash, this implies revenue ₹893.69/₹1,787.39 crore, or 67.33%/92.22% CAGR from FY2026. These are feasibility calculations, not targets. [E23,E24]
Reported 10-/5-/3-year revenue growth of 18.01/34.19/46.59%, coupled with funding and normalization gaps, does not independently support that path. Future dilution raises the enterprise growth requirement. Brand upside is possible, but no funded, independently supported 5×/10× probability is asserted. [E02,E09,E11,E21]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Before lifting the hold, obtain: (1) signed reconciliation of annual versus May/integrated CFO, tax signs, equity proceeds and segment profit; (2) current bank cash, debt/maturities and preferential-proceeds deployment; (3) brand-cost composition, payment records, acquired rights versus internal development/advertising, useful lives, impairment and cohort economics. Reassurance without numbers does not close G2. [E03–E10]
Next results should establish comparable H1 FY2027 sales/collections, consistent brand profits, inventory ageing/markdowns, disputed-receivable recovery and cash after all reinvestment. Check per-share results after the 12.48% preferential share increase, not unadjusted EPS. New information after the cutoff belongs in an update, not this historical record. [E02,E06,E13,E24]
Track Bummer definitive terms, final dilution and closing; Longevity ownership/cash use; overseas incorporation; Centro sell-through rather than association announcements; pending tax outcomes; current pledges/shareholding; and trading lot, spread, depth, surveillance and circuit restrictions. Recompute 20-/60-session liquidity for the actual user position before implementation. [E11–E20]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification: Hold — unresolved. Encompass is a growing but unproven consumer/trading hybrid, not yet an evidence-backed quality compounder. This research is complete at the cutoff with explicit unknowns; the economics are not certified. GOV 4, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 5, CASH 4, BAL 5 and EXEC 5 are independent bounded judgments. CAP/EARN/R remain NS; all aggregate point scores remain NS. G2 prevents ranking; G3 Hold alone does not force quality scores to zero. [E01–E25]
Keep it as a conditional research watchlist candidate until cash, economic earnings and current funding reconcile. Then rebuild returns and actual-position liquidity. Do not convert the illustrative ₹118 entry sensitivity into a purchase limit without those conditions, or buy solely because of a raise, brand announcement or promoter issue price. No trade has been performed.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The claim and primary-source ledgers are embedded and supplied as separate JSON/CSV. Locators are one-based PDF pages unless marked printed page. Official annual/restated statements, exchange announcements and daily NSE archives drive material facts. V denotes verified disclosure, C calculation, M management statement, A analyst assumption. Retrieval dates and document dates are separate; source hashes and fetch scripts preserve provenance. No aggregator or search snippet supplies a final material input.
Open questions: correct CFO and segment profit; economic brand capitalization; current cash/debt/deployment; unit returns, CAC, retention and markdowns; latest free float, pledges and restrictions; GST outcome; acquisition/subsidiary cash obligations; comparable interim results; and quantitative peer comparison. Unknowns remain ND/NS, not zero or neutral 5. Multiples, margins, interim draw, working-capital delays, capex and rescue price are assumptions, not management commitments.
Run python3 build_models.py followed by python3 build_research.py. The bundle contains eleven revenue observations, financial/normalization/IC bridges, annual cash/debt/share paths, reverse expectations, sensitivities, all 13 factors/four gates, 60-session market reconstruction, sources and QA. Model reconstruction needs no network. Large raw source PDFs remain in the working directory; the durable archive contains selected primary PDFs plus extracts, manifests and reproducible inputs. Nothing is published publicly.
